newsitem.title: UK: Elton John joins bid for UK lottery film cash.
newsitem.headline: Elton John joins bid for UK lottery film cash.

text.p: A consortium featuring pop star Elton John is bidding for million of pounds in lottery funding being made available to support British film production, the group said on Tuesday.
John's Rocket Pictures company is part of an eight-member consortium seeking one of four franchises to be awarded by the Arts Council of England.
The Council will award up to 39 million pounds ($64 million) of lottery funding under each of the six-year franchises to encourage the growth of the British cinema industry
Merchant Ivory Productions, a company whose film credits include The Remains Of The Day and A Room With A View, is also part of the consortium.
Other members include music company EMI and British regional television firms HTV and Yorkshire Tyne-Tees.
The consortium plans to produce 34 feature films over the six-year franchise period. Budgets will average 5.3 million pounds for a total investment of 179 million pounds.
The British film industry has enjoyed critical and commercial success in recent year through films such as Four Weddings And A Funeral and Secrets And Lies.

The Arts Council has previously awarded lottery grants to film makers on a one-off basis but now plans to support the industry on a more systematic basis. It will award the grants in late May. ($1=.6107 Pound)
